terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run your file here to see the hours, an incident number and the year's table with its columns lined up.

tasks.title: Hours to one decimal place
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `year_report.py`, write a function called `hours_text` that takes a number of hours, a whole number or a decimal, and gives back a text of that number with exactly one decimal place, rounded, then a space and the letter `h`. For `2.67` it gives back `2.7 h`, and for `4` it gives back `4.0 h`. Print what it gives back for `2.67` and for `4`.

Check calls `hours_text` with numbers of its own, whole numbers among them, and looks at what it gives back.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on decimal places.
Write an f-string with the hours in curly braces.
After the name, inside the braces, say how many decimal places to show.
Try it with a whole number: it should still show one decimal place.
hints: Putting the number in an f-string as it is shows all its decimals, or none for a whole number. `round` keeps a whole number whole.
After the name in the braces, a colon starts the format: a full stop, the number of places and the letter `f`.

tasks.title: An incident number
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, write a function called `incident_id` that takes a year and the number of a callout in that year, both whole numbers, and gives back the incident number: the year, a dash, and the callout's number padded with zeros on the left to three digits. For `2026` and `7` it gives back `2026-007`; a number of three digits or more is not padded. Print what it gives back for `year` and `7`.

Check calls `incident_id` with years and numbers of its own and looks at what it gives back.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on padding with zeros.
Turn the callout's number into text.
Pad that text with zeros to three characters.
Put the year, a dash and the padded number together and give it back.
hints: A whole number has no zeros in front of it until you add them, and `+` between a number and text stops with a `TypeError`.
Text has a method that pads it with zeros on the left to a width you give. The number has to be text first.

tasks.title: One row of the table
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, write a function called `report_row` that takes a hill, a number of callouts and a number of hours, and gives back one row of the table as text: the hill on the left of a column 14 characters wide, the callouts on the right of a column 6 wide, and the hours with one decimal place on the right of a column 8 wide, with nothing else in between. A row is 28 characters long, unless the hill is longer than its column. For `"Carn Dubh"`, `3` and `5.5` it gives back `Carn Dubh          3     5.5`. Print what it gives back for each hill in `by_hill`.

Check calls `report_row` with hills and numbers of its own and looks at what it gives back, space by space.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on widths and alignment.
Write one f-string with three pairs of curly braces.
Give each value its width and its side, and the hours their decimal place too.
Print the rows one under the other and see the columns line up.
hints: Spaces typed between the values only line up when every value has the same length. A width in the format fills the rest of the column with spaces.
In the braces, after a colon, `<` puts a value on the left of its width and `>` on the right. A width and a number of decimal places go together, the width first.

tasks.title: The whole table
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on a table that lines up.
Start the list with the heading line, in the same widths as a row.
Go through the tuples, add a row for each, and keep two totals.
Add the total line after the loop and give back the list.
hints: The heading is text, not numbers, so its columns take a width and a side but no decimal places.
Unpack each tuple into three names in the `for` line, call `report_row` for it, and add its callouts and hours to totals that start at 0 before the loop.

The shape is `lines = [f"{'Hill':<14}{'Calls':>6}{'Hours':>8}"]`, then the loop with `lines.append(report_row(hill, callouts, hours))`, and `lines.append(report_row("Total", all_callouts, all_hours))` after it.
